To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined a novel crystal form of Methanosarcinamazei PylRS, which contains four monomer molecules of PylRS in the asymmetric unit.

we have determined the crystal structures of Methanosarcin mazei PylRS with Boc-Lys-AMP and AMP in the active site, respectively, and that the β7- β8 hairpin structure represents different states in the aminoacyl- tRNA synthesis reaction.

the structures of the four Pyl monomer molecules in the triclinic crystals represent the four different conformational states, i.e. the pre-aminoacylation, pre- and post- aminoacyl-tRNAs, and the BocL-AMPPNP complexes, respectively, and that the conformational change of Asn346, which is located in the active site, accompanies the aminoacyl-transfer reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of the conformational changes that accompany the amino-acid recognition, aminoacylation, pre-aminoacyltRNA synthesis and post aminoacyl-tRNAsynthesis reactions of PylRS.
a novel crystal form of the Boc-Lysyl-tRNA synthase (Pyl-tRNA synthases (PylRSs) from Methanosarcina barkeri (MbPylRS) and Methanosarcina thermophila (MthPylRS).
the structural basis of the conformational changes accompanying aminoacylation and the role of Asn346 in the catalytic reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present structures represent the initial binding, pre-aminoacylation and post-aminoaclylation of the amino acid and that the Asn346 orientation shifts by 85-90o during the catalytic cycle.

the β7-γ8 hairpin structure is involved in the conformational change of the adenylated substrate and the aminoacyl moiety, which occurs during the aminoacyl-AMP formation and aminoacyl-tRNAsynthesis reactions.

the β7-γ8 hairpin is involved in the conformational changes that occur during the aminoacyl-transfer reaction, and that Asn346 is a key residue that participates in the catalysis of aminoacyl-tRNAsynthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformational states in each step of the aminoacylation reaction are captured in the crystal form of PylRS.
the conformational change in the β7-α7 loop of the catalytic subunit is the key to understanding the aminoacyl group transfer reaction of PylRS.
the conformational change of the Asn residue in the catalytically important region is the key factor for the aminoacylation reaction of PylRS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the β7- and β8-strand hairpins of the PylRS dimer are in different conformations, depending on the state of the enzyme, which may be a common feature among aminoacyl-tRNAsynthetases.

the crystal structures of the Boc-Lys-AMP-bound, Boc-Lys AMPPNP-bound and AMP-bound PylRS complexes represent the initial amino acid binding state, the aminoacyl-AMP binding state and the aminoacyl tRNA binding state, respectively.

the β7- and β8-strands, which are located at the tip of a β-hairpin structure in the PylRS active site, are flexible and adopt multiple conformations in response to the binding of substrates and products.
